title: I spent the last 2 months making Cozy Cove, a little pixel-art fishing game you can play in your browser
author: Jonesiller5383
selftext:
Hey everyone! This is the first game I've actually finished, and I wanted to share it.

Cozy Cove is a relaxed top-down fishing adventure around a seaside village. You catch fish, sell them, buy better gear, and that opens up new waters with new fish. Along the way you cook, collect, and dig up the local legends.

What's in it:

\- 39 fish across 8 bodies of water, including two hidden areas I won't spoil

\- A reel-in timing challenge that gets harder for rarer fish, plus six legendary fish

\- Cooking through a fruit-ninja style chopping minigame (13 dishes, each gives a small buff)

\- 30 quests from villagers, a tavern full of regulars, and lore-keepers with their own stories

\- A wizard's tower with a library and a chained-up Forbidden Section you unlock through a quest chain

\- A squirrel dojo with acorn-shuriken throwing and pole balancing

\- An encyclopedia that fills in as you discover fish, ingredients and dishes  


The part I'm proudest of: there are no image or audio files at all. Every sprite, tile and building is drawn in code, and the music and sound effects are synthesized live. The whole game is one HTML file.

It runs in the browser on desktop and mobile, and it autosaves.

  
Try it here:

[https://tesana.com/play/8d052fdd-93a3-4466-a908-083f5f263a80](https://tesana.com/play/8d052fdd-93a3-4466-a908-083f5f263a80)

  
I'd love feedback, especially on the fishing difficulty and whether the early game money feels too slow or too fast. Thanks for looking!

comments.author: TheNutdev
comments.body:
I wish to see size of my Mackerel in the bag!  
Fishing mechanic feels great. I skipped talking to npcs as I wanted to test the fishing right away. Good move that you haven't blocked it by requiring to get through meaningless dialogs.

replies.author: Jonesiller5383
replies.body: That's a really good idea, thanks for the feedback. What do you think of the game?

replies.author: TheNutdev
replies.body: I am huge fan of fishing mini games, like fishing profession in WoW. I find your game entertaining, I am just kinda overwhelmed by the quests and the UI (i understand it might need a polish still). Game didn't autosave for my after closing the browser tab, but maybe I did something wrong.

comments.author: xenofenrir
comments.body: I tested it on mobile,on vertical layout,the dialog displayed on top of the fishing/casting ui,can you take a look?

comments.author: Sojer_96
comments.body: For me it is quite of an acomplishment, no matter if it was built with AI or not. A lot of content after just a two months.

comments.author: Vangrid5857
comments.body: Congrats on finishing your first game!  The hand-drawn-in-code visuals and live-synthesized audio are such clever touch.

replies.author: Jonesiller5383
replies.body: Thanks man! Did you try it?

comments.author: Which-Drop-6797
comments.body: This looks great! Nice job man, played for 20 minutes and had a lot of fun! Feels like a polished Steam release.

comments.author: Ball_Analytics
comments.body: Fr drop this on steam and switch

comments.author: JustRaphiGaming
comments.body: There is already a game called Cozy Grove that's probably a little too close.

comments.author: punikusa
comments.body: When using the fast-moving gauge, the click detection seems off, so no matter how many times I try, it always misses.

replies.author: punikusa
replies.body: When fishing in the sea just south of the initial starting point, there are some difficult fish whose meter moves quickly at randomness about once every 5 to 10 times. I felt that the catch-up detection for those fish was either too tight or off. This is from mobile.

comments.author: FromBiotoDev
comments.body: I made a pixel art game for my girlfriend recently, it's insane the sound effects are nearly identical lol
